newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Continental sells ferry to Canada.
newsitem.headline: Irish Continental sells ferry to Canada.

text.p: Irish Continental Group Plc said on Thursday that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Irish Ferries Limited, has sold the passenger/freight ferry "Isle of Inishturk" to the Canadian ministry of public works and government services for around 6.2 million Irish pounds.
The consideration, which is payable in cash, is equal to the book value of the vessel.
The proceeds will partly be placed on deposit and partly used to repay short-term borrowings, ICG said in a statement.
"The Isle of Inishturk" was replaced on the Rosslare/Pembroke route between Ireland and Wales in March by the "Isle of Innisfree", a vessel with a substantially higher car and freight capacity.

ICG said this transaction, and the return to owners of former chartered-in vessels, form part of Irish Ferries' policy to re-develop its fleet by acquiring substantially larger vessels with enhanced economies of scale.
